_meta.indication: COBENFY is indicated for the treatment of schizophrenia in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, 1:1 to placebo or KarXT, 5-week study with titration to 125 mg/30 mg BID
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in PANSS total score at Week 5
pivotal_trials.result: KarXT superior to placebo in CFB PANSS total score at Week 5 (LS mean difference = -9.6 [95% CI: -13.9, -5.2], p<0.0001)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, 1:1 to placebo or KarXT, 5-week study with titration to 125 mg/30 mg BID
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in PANSS total score at Week 5
pivotal_trials.result: KarXT superior to placebo in CFB PANSS total score at Week 5 (LS mean difference = -8.4 [95% CI: -12.4, -4.3], p<0.0001)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=5% and at least twice placebo) were nausea (19% vs 4%), dyspepsia (18% vs 5%), constipation (17% vs 7%), vomiting (15% vs 1%), hypertension (11% vs 2%), abdominal pain, diarrhea, tachycardia, dizziness, and gastroesophageal reflux disease. COBENFY was associated with a mean increase in 24-hour heart rate of 9.8 bpm.
target_moa: Fixed combination of xanomeline, a muscarinic acetylcholine receptor agonist, and trospium chloride, a muscarinic antagonist. Xanomeline binds and activates muscarinic receptors (M1 to M5) with higher agonist activity at M1 and M4; efficacy in schizophrenia is thought to be due to M1/M4 agonism, while trospium antagonizes peripheral muscarinic receptors to improve tolerability.
modality: Small molecule (fixed-dose combination of two small molecules, xanomeline tartrate and trospium chloride)

boxed_warning.content: No boxed warning; antipsychotic-class boxed warning language was not included. Review PI change table lists BOXED WARNING as 'Not applicable.'

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held; the team agreed outside expertise was not necessary as there were no controversial issues.

basis.text: Breakthrough therapy designation request submitted April 3, 2020 was denied June 1, 2020 because the information did not indicate substantial improvement over existing therapies.

citations.quote: On April 3, 2020, the Applicant submitted a breakthrough therapy designation request. On June 1, 2020, the Division denied the request because the information submitted did not indicate that xanomeline tartrate and trospium chloride demonstrated substantial improvement over existing therapies, specifically regarding its safety and efficacy profile.

basis.text: Priority review was requested but denied; the application was reviewed as standard.

citations.quote: Priority review was requested but denied, as the guidelines for it were not met.

summary.text: NDA 216158 was submitted under the 505(b)(2) pathway relying on trospium chloride (Sanctura) as the listed drug, and reviewed as a standard application. Breakthrough therapy and priority review requests were denied, and no advisory committee meeting was held. The application was approved for the treatment of schizophrenia in adults based on two positive adequate and well-controlled trials.
